# trusted-proxies

<!-- Generated by tools/config-reference.py from libs/platform/src/main/resources/META-INF/oidf-settings/trusted-proxies.json. Do not edit: change the catalogue, then run python3 tools/config-reference.py. -->

The settings of the `trusted-proxies` component of `libs/platform`, read by package `com.pingidentity.ps.oidf.platform.net`: generated from its catalogue, trusted-proxies.json, by `tools/config-reference.py`, and checked in CI. [How to read a row](README.md#reading-a-row).

Families: `OIDF_TRUSTED_`, `OIDF_RATE_LIMIT_`. A name under one of these that no catalogue declares is an unknown key.

Under the production profile a violation by one of these settings refuses `ATTESTATION_AUTH`, `ATTESTATION_ISSUER`, `FEDERATION`, `GM_API`, `OPERATOR_API` (components).

| Setting | Default | What it does | When it's wrong | Profile | Security |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OIDF_TRUSTED_PROXIES` (system property `oidf.trusted.proxies`, then env `OIDF_TRUSTED_PROXIES`) | Unset; a list | The proxies whose forwarding headers are believed, as CIDR ranges or single addresses, space- or comma-separated (10.0.0.0/8, 2001:db8::/32, 192.0.2.7); unset, no forwarding header is believed from anyone. From a listed proxy the client address is the right-most forwarding hop that is not listed, and the scheme and host are what that proxy says: the challenge endpoints', the attester issuance endpoint's and the federation resolve endpoint's per-caller limits, the operator APIs' failed-authentication limit and the attester configuration's and gm-api grant-management metadata's advertised URLs use them | **Doesn't start**: An entry that is not an IPv4 or IPv6 address or CIDR range, or a list of nothing: both challenge endpoints, the attester's issuance and configuration servlets, and the federation endpoints when the resolve endpoint is enabled, are FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and answer 503, and gm-api's metadata servlet does not start; the operator APIs ignore every forwarding header and log the reason at ERROR. A /0 range believes every sender and is logged at WARN | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_TRUSTED_PROXIES_HEADERS` (system property `oidf.trusted.proxies.headers`, then env `OIDF_TRUSTED_PROXIES_HEADERS`) | `x-forwarded`; one of `x-forwarded`, `forwarded` | Which forwarding headers a listed proxy writes: x-forwarded (X-Forwarded-For, -Proto, -Host and -Port) or forwarded (RFC 7239 Forwarded); only that family is read, since a proxy that writes one passes the other through from the client | **Doesn't start**: Not x-forwarded or forwarded, in any case: as OIDF_TRUSTED_PROXIES. The wrong family leaves the client's own header in place, so the client address and advertised URLs are the client's to choose | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_RATE_LIMIT_IPV6_PREFIX` (system property `oidf.rate.limit.ipv6.prefix`, then env `OIDF_RATE_LIMIT_IPV6_PREFIX`) | `64`; a whole number, 32 to 128 | How many leading bits of an IPv6 client address share one per-caller allowance in the challenge endpoints', the attester issuance endpoint's, the federation resolve endpoint's and the operator APIs' rate limits: 64 counts a host's whole /64 as one caller (RFC 7421 section 1), 128 counts each address alone as before 0.7.0. IPv4 and IPv4-mapped addresses are always counted alone, and logs and events still name the full address | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 32 to 128: both challenge endpoints, the attester's issuance and configuration servlets, and the federation endpoints when the resolve endpoint is enabled, are FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and answer 503; gm-api's grant-management metadata servlet, which checks the proxy settings at start, does not start (its init throws, naming the setting), though it keys no rate limit; the operator APIs count IPv6 callers by their /64 and log the reason at ERROR. Too long a prefix gives a client with a /64 a fresh allowance per address; too short makes a whole network share one | Any | Yes |
